findings.message: `read_upload` joins a client-supplied name onto `UPLOAD_DIR` without any check. A value like `../../etc/passwd` or an absolute path escapes the upload directory and can read any file the process can access.
`download` never identifies the requesting user or checks that the file belongs to them. Anyone who knows or guesses a file name can fetch another user's uploads, avatars included.

Several inputs crash the handler with an unhandled exception instead of returning a proper error response. Calling `.decode()` on arbitrary uploaded bytes raises `UnicodeDecodeError` for binary files such as PNGs. A missing file raises `FileNotFoundError`, and an empty or missing `file` parameter resolves to the directory itself and raises `IsADirectoryError`.
The new download behaviour comes with no test, but the contributing guide requires every change in behaviour to have one.
